one_liner: Pylon (usepylon.com) has a REST API with admin-created bearer tokens and an official MCP server (OAuth or API token), but API access needs a paid plan (Professional or higher).
auth_notes: The REST API uses bearer API tokens created by an Admin under Settings > Integrations & dev > API. Tokens don't expire and have no scopes. The vendor's MCP server accepts OAuth 2.0 or an API token, per the current docs. An older support article says OAuth only. No self-serve OAuth app registration is documented for the REST API.
access_notes: A third-party doc (Torii) says API access needs a Professional, Advanced or Enterprise plan. Only Admins can create tokens. No free tier or trial is evidenced in the fetched pages.
blocker_notes: The API is documented, but a working token needs a paid Pylon workspace on Professional or higher. No free tier or trial appears in the fetched pages. A sales-assisted route may exist but is unverified.

evidence.quote: The Pylon API uses [Bearer](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750#section-2.1) authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request
Only Admins can create and manage API tokens.
A Pylon workspace on a plan with API access (Professional, Advanced or Enterprise).
Professional** | **$89 per seat/month**, annual contract | Core support, viewer seats, analytics, automations, Skills, broadcasts, MCP, API, integrations
Developer platform:** REST API, scoped API tokens, webhooks, iFrame embeds, custom apps, Pylon MCP server.
The Pylon MCP Server exposes Pylon data to AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor).
Auth: OAuth 2.0 or an API token.
